document_metadata.jurisdiction_name: Maricopa County / Flood Control District of Maricopa County
document_metadata.document_title: Drainage Policies and Standards Manual for Maricopa County

design_criteria.water_quality_volume_method: Policy 3.6.6 First Flush: retain or treat the first 0.5 inches of direct runoff. Standard 6.10.2 Minimum Design Storm: new developments shall retain stormwater runoff from a 100-year, 2-hour duration storm (retention volume uses P = 100-year, 2-hour rainfall depth). Use with Drainage Design Manual for Maricopa County (Hydrology/Hydraulics/Erosion Control).
peak_flow_calculation_method: Design storm duration criteria (Table 6.2; 6- and 24-hour storms)

evidence.excerpt: Drainage Policies and Standards Manual for Maricopa County
Drainage Design Manual for Maricopa County (DDM)
shall make provisions to retain the stormwater runoff from a 100-year, 2-hour duration storm
The first flush is defined as the first one-half (1/2) inch of direct runoff from the contributing drainage basin.
Analysis confirming basin draining within 36 hours of the end of the design precipitation event is required.
Interceptor channels (and other low impact development techniques, such as: bioswales, microbasins) may be required/needed
Section 323 allows for the use of pervious concrete. Per Section 323 pervious concrete "is usually part of a water management system used to reduce runoff rates and volumes"
evidence.page_or_section: Summary of Changes 6th Edition Draft, Section 2.7.4, page 195

evidence.excerpt: SECTION 6: RETENTION BASINS ... Have stormwater storage and first flush requirements been met?

design_parameters.enrich_notes: First flush WQ volume is 0.5 in direct runoff (glossary; aligns with Policy 3.6.6 in atlas). Retention/storage reports must show basin draining within 36 h after the design precipitation event (6.14.3). Minimum design storm for new development retention is 100-year, 2-hour per Standard 6.10.2 (atlas); rainfall depth not in excerpts. Appendix E/F and Standards 6.10.x (drain time, permeability, drywells) referenced in revision history but numeric SCM criteria largely absent from provided pages.
